source.filename: A6-2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Material constitutive behaviour of all cable components is modeled as linear elastic.
Conductor core (Copper): Young's modulus E = 115 GPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.33.
Insulation layer (XLPE): Young's modulus E = 114 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.45.
Core sheaths (HDPE): Young's modulus E = 932 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.4.
Profile filler (Polymer): Young's modulus E = 1 GPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.4.
Armour wires (Steel): Young's modulus E = 211 GPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3.
Armouring tapes (Polymer): Young's modulus E = 512 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.4.
Outer sheath (MDPE): Young's modulus E = 346 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.44.
Inter-component normal contact is described by a non-linear contact penalty.
Tangential contact follows Coulomb friction with a constant friction coefficient of 0.25 and an elastic slip limit of 0.001.
Analytical formulation assumes fully loxodromic slip (slip occurring in the axial direction along the helical curve) and constant lineload per unit length.
control_variables: Geometric cable parameters: power core lay-angle alpha = 0.12 rad, helical radius R = 27 mm, solid copper conductor cross-sectional area A = 300 mm^2, conductor radius r = 9.8 mm.
FE model length: 1/3 of the cable power core lay-length.
Periodic boundary conditions applied to both ends of the cable segment.
Tangential contact properties: friction coefficient of 0.25 and elastic slip limit of 0.001 across all contact pairs.
Loading sequence: Step 0 (resolve contact), Step 1 (axial tension and radial pressure), Step 2 (reversal/cyclical bending for 2 cycles).
Numerical damping factor: maximum 10^-4 for simulation stabilization during cyclical bending (stabilization energy below 5% of total energy).
dependent_variables: Lineload per unit length acting onto the power cores (kN/m).
Lineload per unit length acting onto the inner sheath (kN/m).
Axial stress history and stress range in the conductor (MPa).
Relative slip between the inner sheath and power cores (axial and radial components, mm).
Relative slip between the inner sheath and armour layer 1 (loxodromic and transverse components, mm).
Shear deformation/strain (gamma_theta_z) in the profile fillers (%).

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A 3D geometrically non-linear finite element model with penalty contact and Coulomb friction was formulated to capture the combined tension, radial pressure, and bending behavior of helically-interwound cores, profile fillers, and sheath layers.

Relative slip between helically wound power cores and the adjacent sheath occurs almost exclusively in the loxodromic (axial) direction due to the small lay-angle, closely matching analytical loxodromic kinematic predictions.

Polymeric profile fillers undergo significant longitudinal shear deformation (up to ~1% shear strain) during cyclic bending, which delays and slows the build-up of friction stresses at low to moderate curvatures.
Internal load-sharing between helically interwound components results in slightly less than one-third of the total inner sheath contact lineload being transmitted to each individual power core.

Analytical models based on loxodromic curves without filler compliance predict a higher axial stress range and faster stress transitions during bending reversals than 3D FE simulations, demonstrating conservatism in analytical stress predictions.

future_work: Development of an analytical formulation for the relative slip and kinematic interactions of helically-interwound power cores.
Use of the 3D FE modeling results to verify and refine analytical formulations for fatigue life assessments of dynamic cables.
independent_variables: Applied radial pressure on the outer sheath (0.2 MPa).
Applied axial strain (0.015%, corresponding to ~90 kN axial tension).
Cyclic bending curvature (amplitudes up to +/- 0.05 m^-1).
Angular position around the cable cross-section (neutral axis at 3 o'clock / theta = 0, top dead center at 12 o'clock / theta = pi/2, bottom dead center at 6 o'clock / theta = -pi/2).
Radial and circumferential evaluation locations within the conductor (outer fibre, center, inner fibre).
limitations_inferred: No physical experimental testing was conducted in this study to independently validate the FE contact, lineload, or slip predictions.
Polymeric components (XLPE, HDPE, MDPE, and profile fillers) are assumed to be linear elastic, omitting rate dependency, viscoelasticity, plasticity, and temperature effects.
The FE model is limited to a 1/3 lay-length segment with periodic boundary conditions, which does not account for boundary disturbances or termination/hang-off constraints.
Simulations are restricted to 2 bending cycles at a single curvature amplitude (+/- 0.05 m^-1) and fixed preloads.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Existing analytical models do not determine contact force distribution between cores and fillers within a three-core cable, requiring either simplified conservative assumptions or FE simulations.
Analytical model formulations do not account for shear deformations in polymeric profile fillers, causing them to overestimate the rate of friction stress build-up at low to moderate curvatures.

Analytical formulations do not accommodate the longitudinal displacement mismatch and opposite-direction sliding of adjacent helically-interwound cores, which leads to earlier slipping than analytically predicted.
main_results: Following the application of tensile strain and radial pressure, the lineload per unit length on each core is uniform around 60 to 63 kN/m, which is slightly less than one-third of the inner sheath lineload (~200 kN/m).

Bending curvature induces minor lineload variations at the top (12 o'clock) and bottom (6 o'clock) positions, while lineload at the neutral axis (3 o'clock) remains essentially unaffected by bending reversals.
Slip of the power cores and first armour layer against the inner sheath is almost purely loxodromic (axial), exhibiting excellent agreement with analytical loxodromic kinematic equations.
Polymeric profile fillers experience shear strain of up to ~1% during bending, softening the friction stress response at initial bending and reversal stages.

Analytical model stress predictions show good overall agreement with 3D FE simulations, but predict a slightly higher stress range and faster initial stress change, confirming analytical conservatism.
At the neutral axis (3 o'clock position), the conductor axial stress variation during bending is negligible, confirming the analytical prediction of zero friction stress at this location.
modeling_methods: 3D finite element (FE) modeling representing 1/3 of the lay-length of the cable power cores incorporating all components (cores, fillers, armour wires, tapes, sheaths).
Geometrically non-linear FE formulation accounting for large rigid body rotations, sliding, and component twisting.
Non-linear penalty contact formulation in the normal direction and Coulomb friction formulation with elastic slip limit in the tangential direction.
Periodic boundary condition formulation applied at both ends of the cable segment.
Analytical modeling of axial stress combining axisymmetric tensile/pressure stress, curvature-change bending stress, and loxodromic stick-slip friction stress.
performance_metrics: Axial stress range and cyclic stress history in the conductor (MPa).
Relative slip distance in axial/loxodromic and transverse/radial directions (mm).
Shear strain percentage in profile fillers (gamma_theta_z, %).
Agreement/discrepancy between analytical stress equations and 3D FE simulation outputs.
possible_gap_implications: Mechanisms of inter-layer loxodromic sliding, contact lineload sharing, and compliant polymeric filler shear could inform mechanics-based modeling of bending stiffness, friction hysteresis, and cable-core slip in multi-lumen continuum robots, flexible steerable catheters, and tendon-driven umbilical conduits.
paper.research_objective: To evaluate the mechanical behavior and stick-slip mechanics of helically-interwound power cores and fillers in a dynamic submarine power cable subjected to combined tension, radial pressure, and cyclic bending using a 3D finite element model, and to assess the accuracy and conservatism of existing analytical formulations based on the loxodromic slip assumption.
paper.research_problem: Dynamic submarine cables undergo cyclic bending, axial tension, and radial pressure during operation, causing fatigue loading where stick-slip friction behavior of helically-interwound power cores plays a critical role, yet existing analytical models assume simplified cylindrical contacts that do not capture intra-layer interactions, filler shear compliance, or interwound core kinematics.
paper.title: BENDING MECHANICS OF CABLE CORES AND FILLERS IN A DYNAMIC SUBMARINE CABLE
